subject_entity.notes: Papias of Hierapolis's five-book exposition c. 95-110 preserved in fragments by Eusebius and Irenaeus; key witness for oral apostolic tradition, teacher succession, Matthew's logia, and millenarianism.

object_entity.notes: Bishop of Hierapolis in Asia Minor; wrote the Exposition of Dominical Oracles (5 books) c. 95-110, preserved by Eusebius; heard John the elder directly; key early witness for oral apostolic tradition and millenarianism.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: Papias says he would not hesitate to expound along with the interpretations whatever he had ever learned from the elders and preserved in memory. He inquired about what the elders said — what Andrew or Peter said, what Philip or Thomas or James, what John or Matthew or any of the Lord's disciples.
passage.notes: Papias deliberately prefers oral tradition from those who knew the apostles; evidence for tradition-reception chain

passage.excerpt: Irenaeus cites Papias: The days will come in which vines shall grow, each having ten thousand branches, each branch having ten thousand twigs, each twig ten thousand shoots, and in each shoot ten thousand clusters. passage.notes: Irenaeus cites Papias for millenarian bodily resurrection hope; confirms Papias learned this from elders who saw John
